European governing body UEFA have been butting heads with Infantino for years and the FIFA boss’ brinkmanship might have finally gone too far. news.title: World Cup 2026 star footballer Vozinha to give up his name as he takes a transfer to Chilean club Colo-Colo
news.lede: After an unforgettable victory against Spain during the course of the FIFA World Cup 2026, Josimar José Évora Dias nicknamed Vozinha not only cemented Cape Verde’s future in football and brought the small Nation to global perspectives, but also emerged as one of the star players of the season by defeating Spain, who then went on to become the Winners. Cape Verde also gave a tough battle to Messi-led Argentina. And in all of the above one name that was instrumental in leadership was that of Vozinha’s. Now, post the World Cup, Vozinha is set to transfer himself from Portuguese club Chaves to Chilean club Colo-Colo.

news.title: Europe is threatening to boycott future World Cups over Gianni Infantino's controversial FIFA plan
news.lede: One of the biggest power struggles in soccer is unfolding behind the scenes, and it could have major consequences for future World Cups. Several European football associations are preparing emergency talks after FIFA unveiled a plan that would allow private investors to buy a minority stake in the commercial business that runs the World Cup. Some officials are even discussing whether a World Cup boycott should be considered if the proposal moves forward. FIFA wants to create a new company called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) that would manage the commercial side of its biggest tournaments, including the FIFA World Cup and Club World Cup.

news.title: Fifa's Infantino plans to sell stakes in World Cup
news.lede: Uefa led the backlash against Fifa after world football's governing body announced plans to seek private investment in the World Cup. Led by president Gianni Infantino, Fifa wants to create a ⁠new commercial subsidiary valued at $20 billion and is seeking backing from its 211 member associations. The plan proposes the creation of the Fifa Forward Enterprise to consolidate the organisation's commercial and event operations. Fifa said it would retain sole control as well as “exclusive authority” over football governance, competitions, the match calendar and all regulatory and sporting decisions.

news.title: Trump links under fresh spotlight as FIFA flags unthinkable sale
news.lede: Updated July 29, 2026 - 2.27am. First published at 12.59am. FIFA’s plans to sell a minority stake that has the potential to reshape the World Cup, the jewel in football’s crown, has been flamed by experts, with president Gianni Infantino in line to profit from the scheme. FIFA announced its plans to create a new commercial subsidiary on Wednesday (AEST) that will operate its main events, like the World Cup, in a move that Infantino claims could triple the amount of money for member associations.

news.title: FIFA boss unveils $US20b plan to sell World Cup to Kushner consortium
news.lede: Gianni Infantino plans to sell the World Cup to a consortium including the brother of Donald Trump's son-in-law. (Getty Images: Chris Brunskill). FIFA president Gianni Infantino is planning to create a $US20 billion company to run the World Cup with private investors. One of the intended investors is Thrive Eternal, a company launched by Joshua Kushner, whose brother Jared Kushner is a son-in-law of US President Donald Trump.

news.title: Burnham blasts FIFA plan to sell World Cup commercial rights
news.lede: “The World Cup is not a product,” said Britain’s prime minister. “Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out.” Prime Minister Andy Burnham has hit out at plans announced by FIFA to sell a chunk of commercial rights linked to the football World Cup. Under the plan, which has provoked a furious reaction from European football association governing body UEFA, FIFA would create an investment vehicle holding commercial rights related to the World Cup and sell a portion of it to investors for $4.2 billion.
